Area.evidence_source: Shame and guilt dominated all the participants. They were ashamed of being victims of sexual violence and experienced a strange sense of guilt. Jonah said, 'There is always this shame... [and] it's [also] shameful for a man to look for help after sexual violence. It belittles your manhood. You are a loser'. Henry recounted: 'You're just so ashamed that it does not even occur to you to ask for help'. Women were perpetrators of four out of seven participants in this study, and it was striking how hard it was for them to come to terms with the fact that they had been raped by a woman. They asked themselves how they could 'let' this happen. They found it more shameful and more difficult to admit because it involved more humiliation, as David said: 'I found it very humiliating [...] I dared not tell any living soul about it'.
